text:
dmitri: Quick heads-up folks  planning ~May 2 -> Jul 1 (about 61 days) to run a field research sprint in Quito, Ecuador. Questions: do I need to declare this as temporary homebase, will the WFH stipend continue, any payroll/tax implications, and can we ship a second laptop + power adaptor?
people-ops: Thanks @dmitri  yes please submit the Homebase Change form (https://redwood.company/forms/homebase) with travel dates and note its a temporary research trip. Stipend usually continues for approved temporary remote and is prorated for partial months.
finance-ops: Stipend proration example we use: "PRORATED = monthly_amount * (days_in_country / days_in_month)". Monthly WFH stipend = $200. For your dates expect full pay for May and prorated for July if you return mid-month. Shipping cap for short trips (temporary equipment) = $1,500; need receipts and customs docs.
tax-eng: Ecuador has specific presence and social security rules. 183-day is a threshold but other activities (meeting customers, hiring, signing contracts) can create higher nexus risk. Field research and interviews are usually low risk but we need details: will you be meeting customers, signing any MOUs, or hiring locally? We'll queue a short nexus check once the Homebase form is in.
dmitri: I will meet with academic partners and attend a public workshop (no sales, no contract signings). No local hiring. Mostly research interviews and collecting usage data.
people-ops: That activity profile sounds low risk but confirms what tax-eng said  we'll still run the tax partner check. Action items: 1) submit Homebase Change form, 2) upload passport + flight, 3) indicate equipment shipping in the form (laptop + power adapter), 4) confirm whether you'll keep US residence for benefits.
it-ship: If you need a second laptop shipped, open a ticket in `#it-ship` with asset tag(s) and Ecuador delivery address. For power adapters we can include universal plugs. Customs in Ecuador often requires a commercial invoice and local import paperwork; employees sometimes pay duties and claim reimbursement. Keep receipts.
finance-ops: Note on payroll: for short approved trips we keep people on USD payroll. If the tax partner flags necessity to route payroll via EOR we will notify you before any routing change. That can change withholding and benefits contributions.
people-ops-bot: Policy update: "Temporary Research & Fieldwork" guidance added to policy hub: https://redwood.company/policies/temporary-remote-research. Checklist includes homebase form, passport copy, local contact, receipts, and nexus review.
people-ops: @dmitri please confirm youll keep your current US address for benefits and whether you want Redwood to pre-pay shipping (we can pre-approve and reimburse) or you prefer to handle customs and claim reimbursement later. We'll start nexus check after form submission and update in ~48 business hours.
dmitri: Keeping US address for benefits. I'd prefer Redwood pre-approve shipping and handle vendor payment if possible  will open `#it-ship` ticket and attach form. Submitted homebase form + passport. Thanks for the quick help! :metal:
